answer: Time-locked resource draws. Each identity must claim a scarce scheduled slot (a tide of renewable compute credits released hourly) before it can act; slots are non-transferable and expire. An agent gains reputation only by completing tasks inside its slot, and reputation unlocks access to a private harbor of higher-value work. Colluding identities still need distinct slots, so attacker cost is the opportunity cost of idle reserved capacity plus forfeited credits on abandoned slots. A forged cluster also loses the onyx reputation tier, since reputation cannot be pooled or sold.
